questions.problem: A cat’s position relative to a fixed origin $O$ is given by the function $x(t)=3{t}^{2}+t$ meters, where $t$ is the time in hours. Find the average position of the cat between $2$ and $4$ hours.
questions.worked_solution:
To calculate the average value of the position on $[{t}_{1},{t}_{2}],$ we use the average value formula

$$
{x}_{\text{avg}}=\frac{1}{{t}_{2}-{t}_{1}}\,{\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}x(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

So, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{4-2}\,{\int }_{2}^{4}(3{t}^{2}+t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{({t}^{3}+\frac{{t}^{2}}{2})|}_{2}^{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[({4}^{3}+\frac{{4}^{2}}{2})-({2}^{3}+\frac{{2}^{2}}{2})] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[(64+8)-(8+2)] \\  & =31.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the average position is $31\,\text{m}.$

questions.problem:
A robotic rover moves in a straight line with velocity 
$v(t)=3{t}^{2}-t,$ where $t$ is measured in seconds and $v$ is measured in meters per second. 

Find the average acceleration ${a}_{\text{avg}}$ of the rover over the time interval $t\in [0,2].$ Do not round your answer.

${a}_{\text{avg}}=$ 
{{field-1}}
${\text{m/s}}^{2}$
questions.worked_solution:
The average acceleration is the average rate of change of the velocity, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{v(b)-v(a)}{b-a} \\  & =\frac{v(2)-v(0)}{2-0} \\  & =\frac{[3(2)^{2}-2]-[3(0)^{2}-0]}{2} \\  & =\frac{(12-2)-0}{2} \\  & =\frac{10}{2} \\  & =5\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the average acceleration is $5\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.$

questions.problem:
A small rover moves along a straight track with velocity 
$v(t)=\sqrt{t}+2,$ where $t$ is measured in seconds and $v$ is measured in meters per second.

Find the average velocity ${v}_{\text{avg}}$ on the interval $[1,4].$ Do not round your answer.

${v}_{\text{avg}}=$ 
{{field-1}}
$\text{m/s}$
questions.worked_solution:
To calculate the average value of the velocity on $[{t}_{1},{t}_{2}],$ we use the average value formula

$$
{v}_{\text{avg}}=\frac{1}{{t}_{2}-{t}_{1}}{\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}v(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

So, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{4-1}{\int }_{1}^{4}(\sqrt{t}+2)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{(\frac{2}{3}{t}^{3/2}+2t)|}_{1}^{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[(\frac{2}{3}\cdot 8+8)-(\frac{2}{3}\cdot 1+2)] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[(\frac{16}{3}+8)-(\frac{2}{3}+2)] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\frac{40}{3}-\frac{8}{3}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(\frac{32}{3}) \\  & =\frac{32}{9}\,\text{m/s}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the average velocity is $\frac{32}{9}\,\text{m/s}.$

questions.problem:
A particle’s acceleration in ${\text{m/s}}^{2}$ is given by the function $a(t)=\sqrt{t},$ where $t$ is the time in seconds.  

Find the average acceleration ${a}_{\text{avg}}$ of the particle on the interval $[1,4].$ Do not round your answer.

${a}_{\text{avg}}=$ 
{{field-1}}
${\text{m/s}}^{2}$
questions.worked_solution:
To calculate the average value of the acceleration on $[{t}_{1},{t}_{2}],$ we use the average value formula

$$
{a}_{\text{avg}}=\frac{1}{{t}_{2}-{t}_{1}}{\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}a(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

So, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{4-1}{\int }_{1}^{4}\sqrt{t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{(\frac{2}{3}{t}^{3/2})|}_{1}^{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[(\frac{2}{3}\cdot 8)-(\frac{2}{3}\cdot 1)] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(\frac{16}{3}-\frac{2}{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(\frac{14}{3}) \\  & =\frac{14}{9}\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the average acceleration is $\frac{14}{9}\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.$
